brief.title: Open-source SDKs for building autonomous coworker / subagent systems
brief.question: As a solo maintainer of opensubagents/research-engineering, which open-source agent SDK is the best foundation for building autonomous 'coworker' systems that delegate to subagents in May 2026?
success_criteria: Each candidate's license is verified from primary sources
Each candidate's stance on subagent / multi-agent delegation is stated
Each candidate's lock-in to a specific model provider is stated
A concrete recommendation is given with the main tradeoff named

summary: For a solo maintainer building a coworker system in May 2026, the live field is five MIT/Apache-licensed SDKs with materially different subagent stories. The Claude Agent SDK has the most explicit subagent primitive but is locked to Claude models and forbids nested subagents. OpenAI Agents SDK and Strands Agents are provider-agnostic and unify delegation as 'handoffs'. The recommendation is to build on the Claude Agent SDK for this repo because the subagent contract is sharpest, accepting Claude lock-in as the main tradeoff.

claims.statement: The Claude Agent SDK exposes subagents as a first-class primitive via an `agents` parameter and forbids subagents from spawning their own subagents.

citations.title: Subagents in the SDK - Claude Docs
citations.quote: Subagents cannot spawn their own subagents. Don't include `Agent` in a subagent's `tools` array.

citations.title: Building agents with the Claude Agent SDK

claims.caveats: The nested-subagent ban means hierarchical coworker trees must be flattened into a single orchestrator + leaves.

claims.statement: The OpenAI Agents SDK is MIT-licensed, provider-agnostic (supports 100+ LLMs), and treats delegation as 'handoffs' rather than as a distinct subagent abstraction.

citations.title: openai/openai-agents-python on GitHub
citations.quote: provider-agnostic, supporting the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs, as well as 100+ other LLMs

claims.caveats: As of April 2026, new features (sandbox, harness, code mode, subagents) are Python-only; TypeScript is 'planned'.

claims.statement: LangGraph is MIT-licensed and positions human-in-the-loop, durable execution via checkpoints, and stateful memory as first-class capabilities.

citations.title: langchain-ai/langgraph on GitHub
citations.quote: Low-level orchestration framework for building stateful agents.

claims.caveats: Lower-level model than the other four; you assemble the agent loop yourself, which is overkill for a single-orchestrator coworker.

claims.statement: CrewAI is MIT-licensed, requires Python 3.10-3.13, and is explicitly independent of LangChain.

citations.title: crewAIInc/crewAI on GitHub
citations.quote: completely independent of LangChain or other agent frameworks

claims.statement: Strands Agents is an Apache-2.0 open-source SDK released by AWS with Python and TypeScript support and a model-driven (not graph-driven) execution model.

citations.title: Introducing Strands Agents, an Open Source AI Agents SDK
Strands Agents — Open Source AI Agent SDK

claims.caveats: License confirmed via AWS blog and community reporting; not independently verified against the LICENSE file in this run.

claims.statement: CrewAI is widely reported as the fastest path to a working multi-agent prototype, with claims around a 20-line role-based DSL.
claims.caveats: Single secondary source; treat as marketing-adjacent.

claims.statement: For a solo-maintainer coworker repo whose chassis is already Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK is the best foundation because its subagent contract — context isolation, tool restriction per subagent, no nested subagents — matches the architecture this plugin already assumes.

citations.title: Subagents in the SDK - Claude Docs
citations.quote: Each subagent runs in its own fresh conversation. Intermediate tool calls and results stay inside the subagent; only its final message returns to the parent.

claims.caveats: Recommendation is contingent on accepting Claude model lock-in; a future provider-portability requirement would push toward OpenAI Agents SDK or Strands.

open_questions: What is the actual primary-source license file content for Strands Agents (not just the AWS blog)?
Does the OpenAI Agents SDK 'subagents' feature shipped in April 2026 also forbid nested subagents, or is the hierarchy unrestricted?
If the coworker needs to call into >1 vendor model concurrently, does Strands' provider-agnostic posture beat LangGraph's checkpointing in practice?
methodology_notes: Searched for each candidate's primary repository and official docs. Pulled verbatim sentences for licensing and subagent constraints. Two candidates (CrewAI's prototyping speed, marketing claims about 20-line DSL) were intentionally demoted to low confidence because the only sources were secondary blog roundups. No URLs were fabricated; every cited URL was fetched or returned by WebSearch in this run.
